direct_claims: This chart shows how the United Kingdom's lighting was sourced from different energy sources between 1700 and 2025.
The sources named on the chart are candles, whale oil, kerosene, gas, and electricity.
The measure shown is share of lighting, expressed as percentages summing to 100% across time.
The chart concerns the history of lighting energy in the United Kingdom, which places it in the domains of energy history, technology transition, and economic history.
The chart is branded by Our World in Data.
The data source line cites Fouquet (2026) and Fouquet and Pearson (2006).
In this chart, a source's percentage represents its share of total lighting use rather than total national energy use.
Because the accessibility metadata is withheld, exact percentages at specific years should not be treated as certain from this description.
The chart spans more than three centuries, so it is useful for understanding long-run technological change rather than short-term fluctuations alone.
